run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T17:13:57Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by HTTP 504 responses produced by the frontend-proxy when the frontend returns slow responses. Over the 73-minute window the frontend-proxy `ingress` (SPAN_KIND_SERVER) series recorded ≈63.98 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans against ≈22,604.77 STATUS_CODE_UNSET ingress spans, and the 5m error ratio rose from 0 at 17:00:57 to 0.0108 (17:16:57) and peaked at 0.0148 (17:18:57) before decaying to 0.0032 (17:24:57). The sampled error spans are `ingress` spans with error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR at ≈15,000,000 µs duration, each paired with a `router frontend egress` child of the same ~15 s duration and http.status_code=0 — an upstream timeout, not an application error. Trace 40fc89a0cadcbbb31ce5939d98b85f7e shows the path: load-generator GET 504 at 15.003 s → frontend-proxy ingress 504 at 15.0018 s → router frontend egress 15.0014 s → frontend `GET /api/recommendations` 15.077 s → `executing api route (pages) /api/recommendations` 15.076 s → client span `grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations` 15.074 s (rpc.grpc.status_code=0), while product-catalog GetProduct calls in the same trace completed in 1.5–2.1 ms. Only the recommendation route was slow: frontend server spans slower than 5 s were 0 for the whole window for GET /, GET /api/data, GET /api/cart, GET /api/products/{productId}, POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout, while GET /api/recommendations reached 0.5481/s at 17:20:57, with its request rate flat at ~0.77–0.81/s. The deepest observed cause is on the single recommendation pod (recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv): container CPU usage (5m rate) rose from ~0.012 cores to 0.0472/0.0814 cores at 17:12:57/17:14:57 and ~0.0955–0.0959 cores through 17:20:57 — the Deployment's 100m CPU limit — while its cgroup throttling ratio rose from a ~0.05 baseline to 0.5161 (17:16:57), 0.8558 (17:18:57) and ~0.964–0.980 through 17:24:57; its own ListRecommendations server-span completion rate fell from 0.7792/s to 0.2889/s (17:14:57) and to 0 from 17:16:57, with no ERROR status series recorded. frontend and frontend-proxy show no resource fault of their own (flat CPU and throttling, both Ready with 0 restarts). Why the recommendation container's CPU demand rose ~8x at ~17:13:57, with no rise in inbound rate, outbound calls or error logs, remains unresolved.

claims.text: frontend-proxy `ingress` (SPAN_KIND_SERVER) spans carry a STATUS_CODE_ERROR series; over the whole query window the increase was ≈63.98 error spans against ≈22,604.77 STATUS_CODE_UNSET ingress spans, while the `router frontend egress` client span series shows 0 STATUS_CODE_ERROR for the same window (its errors carry no status_code).

The frontend-proxy `ingress` error ratio (error spans over all spans, 5m rate) was 0 at 17:00:57, 0.0027 at 17:14:57, 0.0108 at 17:16:57, peaked at 0.0148 at 17:18:57, then fell to 0.0118 (17:20:57), 0.0069 (17:22:57) and 0.0032 (17:24:57); a low baseline of ~0.0004 was present earlier in the window.

The read slice of the error-span result shows frontend-proxy error spans as `ingress` spans with status tags error=true, http.status_code="504", otel.status_code="ERROR" and duration ≈15,000,000 µs (e.g. spans 6b4571fe1450a2e5, 316083acc1064a8c), each paired with a `router frontend egress` child span of the same ~15 s duration with error="true" and http.status_code="0".

In trace 40fc89a0cadcbbb31ce5939d98b85f7e the failing 504 follows a slow frontend recommendation route: load-generator user_get_recommendations 15.004199 s → GET (load-generator) 15.003336 s with http.status_code 504 → frontend-proxy ingress 15.001799 s (504) → router frontend egress 15.001396 s (http.status_code 0) → frontend `GET /api/recommendations` 15.077075 s (http 200) → `executing api route (pages) /api/recommendations` 15.076498 s → `grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations` 15.074102 s with rpc.grpc.status_code="0"; product-catalog GetProduct calls in the same trace took 1.5–2.1 ms.

Within frontend only the recommendation route degraded: the rate of frontend SPAN_KIND_SERVER spans slower than 5 s was 0 for the entire window for GET /, GET /api/data, GET /api/cart, GET /api/products/{productId}, POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout, while for GET /api/recommendations it rose from 0 to 0.0708 (17:14:57), 0.3481 (17:16:57) and 0.5481 (17:20:57); the generic `GET` server span at 0.5185 tracks the same requests.

The frontend request rate for GET /api/recommendations stayed at ~0.77–0.81/s throughout (0.7667 at 17:16:57, 0.7815 at 17:18:57, 0.8111 at 17:20:57, 0.8148 at 17:22:57), so the failure was latency, not an increase in inbound request volume.

CPU usage of the recommendation container (5m rate of container_cpu_usage_seconds_total, pod recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv) rose from ~0.012 cores (0.0121 at 17:10:57, 0.0123 at 17:12:57) to 0.0472 cores at 17:12:57 and 0.0814 at 17:14:57, then ~0.0955–0.0959 cores from 17:16:57 to 17:20:57, easing to 0.0678 (17:22:57) and 0.0298 (17:24:57).

The recommendation pod's cgroup CPU throttling ratio (container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total over container_cpu_cfs_periods_total) rose from a ~0.047–0.054 baseline to 0.5161 (17:16:57) and 0.8558 (17:18:57) and stayed ~0.964–0.980 from 17:20:57 through 17:24:57; in the same series frontend stays ~0.20–0.24, frontend-proxy ~0.030–0.046 and product-catalog ~0.16–0.22.
The recommendation Deployment defines limits cpu=100m / memory=160Mi and requests cpu=30m / memory=80Mi for its single replica, so the observed ~0.096-core usage is at that container's CPU limit.

recommendation's own server span `/oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations` stopped completing: its rate fell from 0.7792/s (17:12:57) to 0.2889/s (17:14:57) and to 0 from 17:16:57 onward; the 5000–15000 ms bucket and the >15000 ms bucket for that series are both 0 for the whole window, so every recorded observation was ≤5000 ms. The same collapse to 0 applies to its `get_product_list` and `/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts` spans.

Only STATUS_CODE_UNSET exists in recommendation's ListRecommendations span-status series (no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series), and recommendation's product-catalog ListProducts child span in trace 40fc89a0cadcbbb31ce5939d98b85f7e appears with parent_is_visible=false, so the corresponding recommendation server span is absent from that trace and recommendation-side duration/status is unknown from the trace sample.

In the returned slice of recommendation logs (the newest 100 of 1490 matching lines, covering 17:16:47–17:19:01), every shown line is 'Receive ListRecommendations for product ids:[...]' arriving at roughly the normal inbound rate; no error, exception or timeout line appears among the shown lines.

recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-p8qtl are both Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and an empty lastState (no terminated container), so no crash, OOM kill or restart occurred on either pod.

The only Kubernetes events returned for otel-demo inside the authorized window belong to fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-dz8j9 (BackOff Warning at 16:53:45, then Pulled/Created/Started Normal at 16:54:00); no Evicted, OOMKilled, Unhealthy or Failed events are returned, and no events are returned for recommendation or frontend-proxy.

product-catalog stayed fast: the rate of its spans slower than 1000 ms was 0 for ListProducts across the whole window and only isolated ~0.0037/s points for GetProduct, and its cgroup throttling ratio stayed in the ~0.16–0.22 band throughout.

recommendation's memory working set (container `recommendation`) rose only from ~42 MB to ~60 MB during the degradation and never approached its 160Mi limit, which is not consistent with memory-pressure eviction.

Primary explanation: the frontend-proxy 504s arise because the recommendation workload's only pod exhausts its 100m CPU limit and is throttled ~97%, so `oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations` takes 15+ s; frontend's `GET /api/recommendations` then exceeds the frontend-proxy 15 s upstream timeout and those 504s are what the RequestErrorRate alert counts. Supporting facts are the near-identical timing (CPU demand rise ~17:13–17:14, throttling and 504-ratio peak 17:16–17:20, both decaying after 17:22), the 15.07 s ListRecommendations client span in the failing trace, and the fact that no other frontend route was slow.

Unresolved trigger: something inside the recommendation pod began consuming roughly 8x its baseline CPU at ~17:13:57 without any increase in inbound requests (frontend GET /api/recommendations flat at ~0.8/s), without new outbound calls (its ListProducts/get_product_list span rate went to 0, not up) and without an error or exception line in the returned logs; candidate mechanisms (internal busy loop/retry, logging or exporter backlog, GC/CPU amplification under the 100m limit) cannot be distinguished with the available telemetry.

The frontend workload was not the bottleneck: its CPU usage (0.062–0.096 cores) and throttling ratio (~0.20–0.27) were flat before and during the incident, its pod had 0 restarts, and all its non-recommendation routes had 0 spans slower than 5 s.

frontend-proxy shows no resource or pod-level fault of its own: container CPU usage was flat at ~0.022–0.024 cores with a ~0.030–0.046 throttling ratio, and the pod is Ready with 0 restarts; its error rate reflects frontend's 15 s responses rather than a fault inside the proxy.

Rejected: product-catalog (recommendation's downstream) caused the slowness. Its spans stayed under 1 s, its CPU throttling was flat, and in the failing trace its GetProduct calls completed in tens of microseconds while the recommendation call was still open.

Rejected: a crash, OOM kill or eviction of the recommendation pod. It is Ready with 0 restarts and an empty lastState, no Evicted/OOMKilled/Failed events are returned for the namespace, and its memory working set (42→60 MB) stayed far below the 160Mi limit.

Rejected as this cause: fraud-detection's BackOff/restart activity (3 restarts, BackOff at 16:53:45, Created/Started 16:54:00) precedes the alert onset at 17:13:57, is not on the /api/recommendations path, and no error spans of the alerting service are tied to it.

Rejected as this cause: recommendation's flagd stream errors. Its `/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream` STATUS_CODE_ERROR series shows only ~0.0037/s at 16:56:57–16:58:57 and 17:04:57–17:06:57 (before the CPU spike and 504 onset) and is 0 from 17:12:57 onward, while `/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean` stayed at 0 error rate throughout.

Review the recommendation Deployment's CPU limit against its actual demand: raise the 100m limit or add replicas so a burst in the single recommendation pod cannot be throttled to ~97%, and add per-container CPU-throttling alerting so throttling is visible before a customer-facing 504.

Capture why recommendation's CPU demand rose at ~17:13:57 — an in-process profile/thread dump or runtime-level CPU/GC metric for the recommendation container during a recurrence — because no returned log line, span or metric currently explains the ~8x demand increase.

gaps: The alerting rule for RequestErrorRate could not be retrieved: list_prometheus_rules returned status no_data both by rule_name (evidence f0d557d6-5ff6-43d4-8ec5-9d8a46993579-t0:f058dc69-7ba3-49cd-9ebe-0e5c493ca63c) and by type=alert (c6a8cc49-0eae-413e-8a7e-711174a21d00-t1:d95b0cc9-097c-41d7-8bb5-cdd96f0380eb, 34f7b722-fee6-4dfb-8b10-cea15495c41a-t1:76b4e76f-3b10-450a-8c78-ab9730ae0b28), so the exact metric, denominator and window behind the reported value 0.06666666666666667 — higher than the 0.0148 peak ingress error ratio measured here — are unverified.

The reason recommendation's CPU demand rose ~8x at ~17:13:57 is unknown; no application-level metric, profile or error log line in this Run explains it, and recommendation's own server spans are absent from the sampled trace and stop being recorded after ~17:15.

The log-exclusion query on recommendation returned status no_data (103d0d03-d41d-4dc4-8354-c902fd0571c1-t0:7d8ba783-f1d3-412e-b90c-afe7976a4f5d), so 'no non-request log lines were emitted' is unconfirmed; only the returned 100 newest of 1490 lines (027cc46e-af29-4880-875a-ebe93de6d7f3-t0:576fa88d-b4d3-4349-a5e5-3760f763279b) were seen, and lines after 17:19:01 were not read.

frontend pod logs could not be read: fetch_pod_logs returned status no_data for frontend-675fd7b5c5-x7pxv (a272f18c-90a0-4afa-939a-8615c8caeacb-t0:6c0d5038-fa17-4948-87bf-dcbca452ede5 and 61e9c098-c012-4828-929a-1448756714fb-t1:628e6aa3-5ac2-4e62-93c4-925ab93971e8), so frontend-side gRPC deadline or retry messages are unknown, not absent.

The error-span result was truncated and only the first 40 of 340 rows were read (c6a8cc49-0eae-413e-8a7e-711174a21d00-t0:715a3849-c1a3-4b7f-942c-e7c572c8d3b0); error spans outside 17:15:35–17:19:50 were not inspected.

The 504-specific trace search returned status no_data (f0d557d6-5ff6-43d4-8ec5-9d8a46993579-t2:949873f4-5678-463f-a764-1f3257cd1ae2), so no direct confirmation of any status-500 path exists either way.

Querying deployment replica readiness returned status no_data (311dd753-884a-4bf3-a404-618f75bb1e1e-t2:4b3c1814-cf7a-4647-a106-225bd61d1870) and product-catalog ERROR spans returned status no_data (311dd753-884a-4bf3-a404-618f75bb1e1e-t1:29c55de6-3e7d-4741-8a5a-e69c218f428f); missing series here are unknown rather than zero.

The span-metric series listing for frontend was capped at 100 entries (5f972cbe-a77f-4a43-8c14-998bbe929d29-t1:b101a757-4660-4f8c-92a3-77c51930eb6d), so complete label coverage of frontend duration buckets is unknown.

change_history is not integrated in this Run, so the namespace-wide pod creation at ~16:32:34–16:32:38 (recommendation started 16:32:36, about 41 minutes before the alert) cannot be tied to a change or excluded as a latent factor.

Node-level CPU/steal for the node hosting recommendation (i-07fdfccf76e0651ab) was not examined, so node contention cannot be fully excluded even though no other pod on that node shows a throttling change.
next_steps: Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule definition from Alertmanager/Prometheus rule files to confirm the exact metric, denominator and evaluation window, and reconcile it with the 0.0148 peak ingress ratio measured here.
Inspect the recommendation container's runtime profiling or thread/GC data during a recurrence to identify what drove the ~8x CPU demand increase at ~17:13:57.
Read recommendation logs before 17:16:47 and after 17:19:01, and read frontend pod logs, once log access succeeds, to check for deadline-exceeded or retry messages.
Consult change history for the otel-demo namespace around 16:32 and 17:13 to establish whether the pod roll-out or a config change relates to the CPU demand shift.
Evaluate raising or removing the recommendation container's 100m CPU limit (or scaling past one replica) so bursts cannot be throttled to ~97%.

Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.
